title: Linux monitoring agent footprint benchmark (2026): 11 agents, one VPS type, 24 hours

run.plan: CX23: 2 vCPU AMD EPYC (shared), 4 GB RAM, 40 GB NVMe
notes: Ubuntu's apt-daily and apt-daily-upgrade timers were masked on every box at provisioning (the pilot's unattended-upgrades restarted dynamically linked agents mid-cycle).
Network bytes count only the box's physical interfaces; Docker bridge traffic is excluded.
Processes are counted in the agent's cgroup and its child cgroups.

metrics.label: Memory (PSS) peak, first hour after install
CPU, under load (% of one vCPU)
Log volume handed to journald per 24 h
Network per 24 h (out for push agents, in+out for polled)

rows.name: HetrixTools agent
footnotes: This box has no cron, so the vendor installer's own systemd path runs: a minutely timer starting a transient unit per run. Those runs are placed in a persistent slice (one word added to the vendor launcher) so the kernel's accounting for them survives each run; the timer's launcher unit is counted too.

The CPU figure (13 to 17 % of one vCPU) is the same in all three runs and agrees with the box's load average: its idle median is 0.22 to 0.30 on this row's boxes against 0.05 to 0.12 on every other box.

rows.name: Beszel agent
rows.reportsTo: Beszel hub on the sink (WebSocket, hub-driven every 60 s)
footnotes: Run 3 (box-6): this run's 15.1 MB of disk writes all fall in the first 7.0 hours after the install and then stop; in that span the agent logged nothing, its on-disk footprint did not grow, and its CPU, memory and network figures are the same as in the hours after. The same writes (the same hourly rate and block sizes, about 16 MB in all) appear in one run of another agent on another box and day (Monitorable, run 1) and in neither agent's other two runs, so they are most likely the box's filesystem writeback charged to this unit's cgroup, not the agent's own writes. The cause is not established; the figure is published as measured.

rows.name: node_exporter
rows.reportsTo: passive: Prometheus on the sink scrapes /metrics at its default 1 m
footnotes: Network bytes are counted by TCP port (the listening socket is not in the service's cgroup under socket activation, and polled traffic is what this row sends).

rows.name: Monitorable agent
footnotes: Run 1 (box-1): this run's 14.5 MB of disk writes all fall in the first 7.8 hours after the install and then stop; in that span the agent logged nothing, its on-disk footprint did not grow, and its CPU, memory and network figures are the same as in the hours after. The same writes (the same hourly rate and block sizes, about 16 MB in all) appear in one run of another agent on another box and day (Beszel, run 3) and in neither agent's other two runs, so they are most likely the box's filesystem writeback charged to this unit's cgroup, not the agent's own writes. The cause is not established; the figure is published as measured.

Run 3 (box-7): the 0.3 MB are the agent's export queue. A batch that is not delivered within 15 s is written to disk; that happened between 16:24 and 21:16 UTC on 2026-11-11, hours in which exports timed out or were answered "unavailable" and were retried. A run in which every batch is delivered in time writes nothing (run 2).

rows.name: Pulse agent
rows.reportsTo: Pulse server on the sink (HTTP push every 30 s)
footnotes: Auto-update stays at its default (on).

The agent talks to the Pulse server over the bed's private network (10.0.0.0/24) in plain HTTP: the agent refuses an http:// server URL unless the host is loopback or a private address, and the sink has no TLS hostname. The installer it fetches from the server is checksum-pinned.

rows.name: Glances
rows.reportsTo: passive: the sink polls /api/4/all at Glances' refresh period
footnotes: Glances ships no systemd unit; the harness adds a two-line one that runs `glances -w`.
Runs as root (pipx install as root, the documented route); port 61208 is reachable from the sink only.
Network bytes are counted by TCP port (the listening socket is not in the service's cgroup under socket activation, and polled traffic is what this row sends).

The network figure is the harness's own poller fetching /api/4/all every 3 s (Glances' refresh period); each reply is about 137 KB, which is the 3.9 GB per 24 h. Scale it to your own polling interval.

rows.name: Telegraf
rows.reportsTo: InfluxDB 1.x on the sink (the stock [[outputs.influxdb]] block, enabled with the sink's URL)
footnotes: Telegraf's stock config enables no output; its [[outputs.influxdb]] block is enabled with the sink's URL (two lines). Nothing else is changed.

rows.name: Datadog Agent
footnotes: Every datadog-agent* unit is summed (7.84+ runs a process manager).
The memory peak is the sum of each datadog-agent* unit's own high-water mark over the cycle; those peaks did not happen at the same moment, so the figure overstates the coincident peak.
Run 3 (box-4) installed Agent 7.85.3; runs 1 and 2 installed 7.85.2. The vendor's documented install takes the release that is current at install time.

rows.name: Netdata (self-hosted)
rows.reportsTo: nothing (standalone; local dashboard on :19999, not opened)
footnotes: ML anomaly detection stays at its default (on).
kickstart's default channel is nightly; installed with --stable-channel so the version is a release readers can reproduce.
Anonymous telemetry and the daily updater timer stay at their defaults; the updater's unit is counted with the agent.

rows.name: Netdata (claimed to Netdata Cloud)
footnotes: Same binary as the self-hosted row, claimed to Netdata Cloud. ML anomaly detection stays at its default (on).
kickstart's default channel is nightly; installed with --stable-channel so the version is a release readers can reproduce.
Anonymous telemetry and the daily updater timer stay at their defaults; the updater's unit is counted with the agent.

control.name: No agent (harness only)
control.reportsTo: nothing: the control box measures the harness itself
footnotes: Control row: no agent; the collector measures its own cgroup.
